hypotheses.justification: The statement still holds without hv. Refines n q p only says: for i < n, p.cst[i]! = i → q.cst[i]! = i. If n = 0 this is vacuous. Otherwise, if v ≥ n, then since hp.posSize gives p.pos.size = n ≤ v, p.pos[v]! is the default 0. So the split cell is the one containing position 0, with c = p.cst[0]! ≤ 0 by hp.cstLe, so c = 0, and ec = p.cen[0]!. By individualize_cst_eq and setCstFrom_getElemD (which needs only ec ≤ p.cst.size, from hp.cenLe and hp.cstSize), the new cst[k]! is 1 if 1 ≤ k < ec, and p.cst[k]! otherwise. Suppose p.cst[i]! = i with 1 ≤ i < ec. Then hp.cellCst at index 0 gives p.cst[i]! = p.cst[0]! = 0, so i = 0, a contradiction. So the new cst[i]! = p.cst[i]! = i in every case. For v < n the existing proof applies unchanged. In the proof, hv is used only to build IndivData, so a case split on v < n replaces that step. The out-of-range case is the short argument above, done directly with individualize_cst_eq and setCstFrom_getElemD. hp is still needed: for an arbitrary Part the cst array could have a cell start inside the split interval.
